title: Shalom Aleichem
program_note:
Shalom Aleichem is a treatment for string quartet of the hymn tune originally written by Rabbi Israel Goldfarb in New York City about a century ago, as a setting of the words written by an anonymous kabbalist about three or four centuries earlier. It is dedicated to Cantor Joseph Gole, cantor of Sinai Temple, on the occasion of its founding one century ago.

The music begins with passionate, fervent, prayer-like melodies, which gradually coalesce into a setting of the Shalom Aleichem melody. Through the course of this setting, containing reminiscences of other melodies, the passion gradually cools, and the principal hope of the prayer comes through: peace be unto us all.

The composition is approximately 5:15 in duration.  It was later incorporated into the piano quintet Dreams, All of a Peace.
